<thought>From the measurements, all nodes lie on a single linear path between terminals A and B. The resistance from A to each node gives its position along the line. By ordering the nodes by their measured resistance from A, the differences between successive nodes give the individual resistor values. The ordered nodes and the computed resistor values are:

- A (0 Ω)
- X1 (6.667 Ω)  R1 = 6.667 Ω  (A‑X1)
- N_b1 (11.667 Ω) R2 = 5.000 Ω  (X1‑N_b1)
- N_b2 (21.667 Ω) R3 = 10.000 Ω (N_b1‑N_b2)
- N_b3 (36.667 Ω) R4 = 15.000 Ω (N_b2‑N_b3)
- X2 (56.667 Ω)  R5 = 20.000 Ω (N_b3‑X2)
- N_c1 (61.667 Ω) R6 = 5.000 Ω  (X2‑N_c1)
- N_c2 (71.667 Ω) R7 = 10.000 Ω (N_c1‑N_c2)
- N_c3 (86.667 Ω) R8 = 15.000 Ω (N_c2‑N_c3)
- X3 (106.667 Ω) R9 = 20.000 Ω (N_c3‑X3)
- N_d1 (116.667 Ω) R10 = 10.000 Ω (X3‑N_d1)
- N_d2 (131.667 Ω) R11 = 15.000 Ω (N_d1‑N_d2)
- B (151.667 Ω)  R12 = 20.000 Ω (N_d2‑B)

All other measured resistances are consistent with the sum of the appropriate series segments, confirming that the circuit is a single series chain with taps at the listed nodes.
